acquisition_method.evidence: experiment types: Shotgun proteomics; Gel-based experiment

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Alkylation was conducted by replacing the DTT solution with 55 mm IAA (Sigma) and incubated at 22 °C for 20 min in the dark

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Our results indicate that a simultaneous and short, high temperature reduction and alkylation reaction using Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine hydrochloride (TCEP) and chloroacetamide (CAA) with a subsequent gel wash improve protein identification and sequence coverage, diminish peptide side reactions.

cleavage_agent.evidence: The gel pieces were hydrated with minimum volume required of 2.5 ng μL–1 of trypsin (Promega) in 50 mm ABC solution, pH 8 for 1 h at room temperature, topped up with ABC solution until the gel pieces were covered and incubated overnight at 37 °C.

collision_energy.evidence: Precursor ions were fragmented with higher energy C‐trap dissociation (HCD), normalised collision energy of 33% and fixed first mass of 120 m/z.

fragmentation_method.evidence: Precursor ions were fragmented with higher energy C‐trap dissociation (HCD), normalised collision energy of 33% and fixed first mass of 120 m/z.

ionization_type.evidence: Electrospray used a static Nanospray‐Flex with a stainless steel emitter OD 1/32’ in positive mode at 2.1 kV (Thermo‐Scientific).

mass_analyzer.evidence: MS survey scans from 375 to 1575 m/z, with a 2 × 105 ion count target, maximum injection time of 150 ms, and resolution of 120 000 at 200 m/z, acquired in profile mode were performed in the Orbitrap analyser.

ptm.evidence: modifications: acetylated residue; iodoacetamide derivatized residue

reduction_concentration.evidence: dehydrated gel pieces were reduced with 10 mm DTT (Sigma) at 56 °C for 30 min.
